set.approach: The route is reached by crossing the Dione Glacier below the peak. Expect a bergschrund at the base of the climb, where a screw or a picket helps.
set.descent_text: Descend by reversing the line of ascent.

review.notes: Dione Glacier approach from area page; route-page topo caption recommends reversing the ascent. Thin; single source each.

set.descent_text: From the top, downclimb to the neck between the head and the body rather than trusting the rusty old piton at the summit. From the neck, rappel to the base using the block and slings there; carry fresh webbing to back them up.

review.notes: Standard route on the Camel per club wiki; matches 5.2 grade. Single source.

set.descent_text: The route tops out on the South Peak, where the line joins the West Buttress. Descend by the south ridge of the South Peak, the same way as the West Buttress descent.

review.notes: Route page gives its top-out and descent in one line; single source.

set.approach: From the Valhalla trail system, climb the gully that runs between the Muzzle and the Wolfs Ears, rather than a farther col, to reach the basin below the ears. Helix starts on grassy ledges on the left side of the West Ear's south face, left of the Pack, and follows bolted belays up the face to the summit.
set.descent_text: Descend from the summit by the west side: short rappels from bolted anchors and some scrambling drop to the sand gully west of the summit, which is a third-class walk back toward camp. Manage the ropes carefully, as they snag easily. Partway up, a traverse left leads into the same descent gully if a retreat is needed.

review.notes: Approach gully between Muzzle and Wolfs Ears: Helix page + blog + photo caption. Descent: sand gully west of summit after rappels, blog + MP caption; no rappel count given.

set.descent_text: Descend by the standard line down the west ridge of the West Ear, which uses a couple of short rappels or some downclimbing into the gully west of the summit. From the top of the fourth pitch you can instead rappel the route; every station has bolted anchors, and a long single rope or two ropes reaches between them.

review.notes: Pack page states west-ridge descent and rappel of the route; blog confirms gully west of summit. Counts of rappels omitted.
